learning_outcomes.title: Law of Sines and the ambiguous case
learning_outcomes.statement: Determine whether three given measures define 0, 1, or 2 triangles using the Law of Sines.
learning_outcomes.rule_summary: Use a/sin A = b/sin B. For SSA, sin B = b sin A/a. Test both B₁ = sin⁻¹(value) and B₂ = 180° − B₁, accepting only cases with A + B < 180°. Opposite sides and angles share letters.

questions.instruction: Determine whether the triangle has no solution, one solution or two solutions. Then solve it. Round sides to the nearest tenth and angles to the nearest degree.
questions.stem: Determine whether the triangle has no solution, one solution or two solutions. Then solve it. Round sides to the nearest tenth and angles to the nearest degree. A=50^\circ,\quad a=34,\quad b=40

parts.prompt: Determine the number of solutions and justify it.

answer.model_answer_and_marking: sin B=b sin A/a=0.90122876. Two solutions; test both arcsine candidates against A+B<180°. Correct ratio (2), count and admissibility (2).

parts.prompt: Give every possible triangle, or explain why none exists.

answer.model_answer_and_marking: B≈64°, C≈66°, c≈40.4; B≈116°, C≈14°, c≈11.0 Calculate with full-precision angles before rounding. Correct possible triangles and remaining side(s) (6).
